details:
Running two VRChat clients on the same PC (the second launched with --osc=9010:localhost:9011 to avoid a port clash) makes both clients log this line about every 5 seconds:

  no SRV Records found in not parse answer from <own IP>:5353

That works out to about 1,260 lines per hour per client. With only one client running, the line never appears.

After the second client exits, the remaining client keeps logging it every 10 seconds, even though the only mDNS answers it now receives are its own. It stops only when that client is restarted.

The mDNS answers themselves look fine. A capture shows each one has the PTR record in Answers, and the SRV, TXT and A records in Additional Records.

What I found in vrc-oscquery-lib (MeaModDiscovery.cs):

- The message is not about missing SRV records. It is the fixed text of a catch block around AddMatchedService/RemoveMatchedService, and the exception itself is not logged.

- In AddMatchedService, the OSCQuery duplicate check is `!sp.name.Equals(profile.InstanceName)`. This compares a string with a MeaMod DomainName, so it is always false. As a result, OnOscQueryServiceAdded fires for every OSCQuery answer, including repeats and the client's own service. The OSC branch uses `!=` and works correctly.

- Running the library standalone confirms this: OnOscQueryServiceAdded fires on every answer. In VRChat, the number of log lines matches the number of extra OSCQuery services visible on the network, so the exception seems to be thrown by VRChat's handler for that event.

- Open PR #60 (https://github.com/vrchat-community/vrc-oscquery-lib/pull/60) fixes this check and has been open since March 2024.

Suggested fixes:

1. Merge PR #60, or an equivalent fix, into the library that VRChat ships.

2. Include the exception in that catch log, or use a message that reflects what actually failed.

Environment: VRChat 2026.3.3p1-1920, Windows 11, both clients on the same PC and NIC.
title: OSCQuery: "no SRV Records found" log spam with two clients on one PC
